explain.say: Imagine laws deciding where you live, which school you go to, even which beach you may use, all because of your skin colour. In South Africa that system was called apartheid, which means apartness. The timeline shows how it was defeated. Let's walk it.

faq.a: Apartheid, meaning apartness in Afrikaans, was a system of laws in South Africa from 1948 to the early 1990s that separated people by race and kept power and the best land, jobs and schools for white people.
On 21 March 1960, police fired on a crowd protesting against pass laws in Sharpeville, killing 69 people. The date is now Human Rights Day in South Africa.

faq.q: Why was Nelson Mandela in prison?
faq.a: Mandela, an ANC leader, helped start an armed wing after peaceful protest was banned. In 1964, at the Rivonia Trial, he was sentenced to life imprisonment. He spent 27 years in prison, many of them on Robben Island.
asks: How long was Mandela in prison?

faq.q: How did the world help end apartheid?
faq.a: Many countries and people boycotted South African goods, sport and culture, and governments imposed sanctions. Together with protests inside South Africa, this pressure pushed the government to negotiate.
asks: What were the sanctions against South Africa?

faq.a: Apartheid laws were repealed in 1990 and 1991, and South Africa held its first election open to all races on 27 April 1994. Nelson Mandela became the first Black president.

facts: Nelson Mandela was released from prison on 11 February 1990 after 27 years.
South Africa's first democratic election was held on 27 April 1994.
Police killed 69 people at Sharpeville on 21 March 1960.

quiz.say: What does the word apartheid mean?
quiz.why: In Afrikaans, apartheid means apartness, the separation of people by race.

wrong.1: Apartheid was the opposite of freedom.
wrong.2: Apartheid kept people apart, the opposite of friendship.

quiz.why: People of all races voted together for the first time.

wrong.1: Mandela was jailed in 1964 and freed in 1990.
